resources.string: Brightness that keeps up with the room.
Off, so the system is deciding the brightness.
Screen off, so the light sensor is parked.
Following the room, but the system is doing the ramping.
On, LuxRamp reads the light sensor itself and moves the screen at a speed you choose, instead of waiting for the system to notice the room changed.
Shizuku is not connected, so brightness goes through the system and the system ramps it. Everything still works, it is just no longer instant.
How long the screen takes to move, once LuxRamp has decided to move it.
How readily LuxRamp believes the light in the room really changed.
Where the whole curve sits, for eyes that are not average.
How long the screen takes to reach a brighter level. Shorter feels instant, longer feels calmer.
How long it takes to dim. Slower is usually better, because dimming you notice is dimming that annoys.
How quickly LuxRamp believes the room got brighter. Lower reacts sooner but can chase a passing light.
How quickly it believes the room got darker. Higher keeps a shadow crossing the sensor from dimming the screen.
Your overall preference. Higher is brighter everywhere, and it lifts dim rooms the most.
